[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Ever since I saw the reveal, I fell in love with the design as it is very futuristic. The fit is true to size as I have wide feet and the toe box gave me more than enough room. Also, it does not need any break-in at all!! The moment I put these on, I immediately felt the comfort compared to the 90s, 97s, and other air maxes which needed a couple of wears for you to feel the most comfort. The air bubbles combined with the foam around it make more comfortable. I did notice that PSI differences from what was advertised and I’m very satisfied with the comfort. I think a heavier person would feel it more as I’m 6ft 185 pounds. I feel more comfort of the air bubbles when I’m doing heavy lifting while walking. I often end up having to stand still for a long time and these are very good for it! This shoe is a better version of the air max 90!
 The upper materials look really cool and are comfortable enough that it doesn’t squish your toes, especially when wanting to move your toes around. I like the patent leather design on the front of the toe box. It has Very good arch support. The tongue is very comfortable as it has a lot of padding. 
I am loving the outsole design as it is my new favorite from the air max line. From the outsole to the heel reminds me of a military tank but on your feet. I like the glossy design on the side with the swoosh as it is present on the heel as well. 

 There’s only a few cons I have with the shoe that I would change is the design of the tongue and the materials for the laces. The tongue is very comfortable but I’m not too fond of it as it doesn’t look like it fits with the rest of the shoe. It looks a bit “outdated” for what it aiming for with the futuristic design. It reminds me of the air max 270, air max pulse which I also didn’t like the tongue design of those either. However, I do love the “glossy/trippy” look of the air max logo on the tongue and I would like for that to come back in future shoes! 
The materials for the laces reminds me of the Pegasus 39 as it keeps coming unlaced which gets annoying having to tie it often. I never had any lacing problems other than the Pegasus 39 and this new air max DN. I had to double lace. it is very minor and did not hinder the experience.

The air max DN is the best of the air max line to have released in recent years. I hope more people like this shoe enough that it’ll keep on selling longer than previous models. I received many compliments when wearing this shoe and I have couple friends that even bought the shoe because they liked how it looked as well. I can’t for all of us to match wearing the newest air max!

raw_title: Like Air for Both Athletes and Fashionistas
raw_review_text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] These sneakers immediately became one of my top favorites. Out of all the 10 sneakers I have from Nike, this Air Max Dn pair is in my top 3 in terms of comfort. Comfort is the most important factor for me regarding shoes, and I would say this is as comfortable as Nike's other similar line of sneakers (think VaporMax and Jordan Delta). These have that "walking on air" quality to them, in a way that propels you smoothly and easily as you walk. You can stand and walk in these for hours without experiencing foot pain after. My right foot is wider than my left, which is more vulnerable to pain if wearing certain shoes, but these have a stretchy quality that hugs your feet so right they are unnoticeable. The foam provides cushion and support, and the seams do not rub against your ankle which would irritate the skin. They are lightweight and not heavy, making walking feel as if you're gliding. I think these would be suitable for a variety of foot shapes, such as wide or narrow shapes and flat or curved shapes.
The Air Max Dn would be a great running shoe for both the treadmill or outside running and other activities that require you to react quickly with your feet such as boxing a heavy bag at the gym. I would also wear these for golfing and playing laser tag. You can wear these for weightlifting too, but I personally would not wear these for most leg workouts due to the sneaker's design. It has that running shoe design and is therefore not flat enough to be well-balanced to perform squats and other leg workouts. I do not know if these sneakers will be suitable for other sports as the ones I mentioned are those I regularly participate in, though I don't see why they wouldn't be great for dancing as well. The tread pattern provides enough grip for any of these activities.
The material of these is nice too and it looks sporty. The layered mesh is lightweight and will be easy to clean. The mesh doesn't seem to capture and hold onto dirt easily, so wiping them clean with a damp cloth is often enough. It's breathable and does not make your feet feel hot after wearing them for hours. I've walked a lot in these on a hot day (I am based in California) and did not feel uncomfortably hot or grossly sweaty after wearing them for over 6 hours. The material of the laces has a good grip and does not seem to become untied easily. They feel durable and are of good quality. I can see these lasting for years even after wearing them for many activities, like with my other Nike sneakers. Like the VaporMax line, the materials used were recycled.
Aside from the design in terms of comfort, fit, and activity suitability, these look cool and cute when paired with all sorts of outfits. They look great with flared pants or leggings, straight-cut denim jeans or shorts, tennis skirts, joggers, and gym leggings. I love the bubble design (especially under sunlight) and Nike swoosh design on the sole, and the back of the sole looks cool too. They're just incredibly versatile. I definitely want another pair in a different color. The glossy accents are reflective, which is helpful for safety and possibly for individuals with sensory sensitivities.
The only thing I would change is to add a little tie or hook on the back for your finger to hold onto so that it is easier and faster to put on. They require you to loosen the laces in the upper mid area of the shoe to be able to fit in them. There's no leather to worry about creasing, but I would still take a few seconds to fit my feet in them properly. They are still easy to slip into, which could benefit individuals with limited mobility. Swapping the laces with no-tie laces could also help improve accessibility and preference.

raw_review_text: Just passing this along for others who may have been fans of the original Club C shoes and were hoping to get new ones of the same design. While these are generally similar, there have been some small cosmetic and some more meaningful changes. I still have a couple of pair that I had bought and held onto from years ago, and included a comparison in the photos. The new versions  (despite the Vintage or Vintage TV names) have a different stitch pattern on the side, and are also cut so that there is less coverage and support of the foot around the ankle (the leather on the new version extends 2 inches up from the top of the sole while the older model was 2.5 inches at the same location). More difficult to capture in a photo is the fact that the original version had a pretty substantial arch support that adds good support and comfort for long walks and heavier use. The new version is almost flat inside the sole, not unlike the old 1970s canvas sneakers from another brand, with little if any arch support (the difference is striking). Finally, another notable difference is that there was a "wide" sizing available before, which I cannot seem to find for any of the current Club C models. All of that said, I am reasonably satisfied with the new ones, but would be much more so if they matched the construction, size and shape specifications of the older versions of the same shoe.

raw_review_text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’ve always admired the iconic design of the Adidas Samba OG, and visually, they live up to the hype. The materials feel high quality, and the shoes are lightweight and versatile—perfect for casual wear and street style. However, once I started walking in them, I noticed a major downside: lack of support.

At size 7.5, the fit was true to size, but I felt a surprising lack of stability—almost like I was off balance. The flat sole doesn’t offer much in terms of arch or heel support, which made longer walks uncomfortable. It felt like my feet were working harder to stay stable.

To address this, I added my own inserts to give the shoes a bit more structure and cushioning. That helped significantly, but I do think a shoe at this price point should offer better support right out of the box.

If you’re someone who values foot support or has flat feet, I’d recommend planning to add your own orthotics. Otherwise, this is a beautifully designed shoe that nails the retro aesthetic.

I don’t know if the sole would get more flexible over time, but it was too stiff for me to want to choose this as my go-to exercising shoe. 

Overall I think it’s a cool shoe with that classic nike shox look, but I wouldn’t choose it for regular exercise.

[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I recently picked up a pair of Nike Shox R4 in the all-black colorway, and I have to say, I love the sleek, minimalist design. The all-black aesthetic works perfectly for someone like me who prefers more subdued tones over bright, flashy colors. The style definitely catches the eye, making them a solid option for casual wear.

However, after wearing them for a few days, I’m realizing these shoes may not be the best choice for running. I ordered a size 8, and while they fit well in terms of length, I’m thinking I should have gone half a size down. The extra room in the toe box made them feel slightly less secure, especially when moving at faster speeds. 

Speaking of movement, the weight of the Shox R4 is something I really noticed during my runs. These shoes are on the heavier side, and the Shox technology, while providing some cushioning, didn't give me the light, responsive feel I prefer for running. I found myself running and walking a bit awkwardly due to the added bulk, which made the experience less comfortable than expected.

That said, these shoes do excel in everyday wear. They're stylish, comfortable enough for casual use, and have a unique look that sets them apart from other sneakers. If you’re looking for a pair of shoes to wear around town or for light activities, they’ll do the job just fine. But for intense workouts or running, I would suggest looking for something lighter and more performance-oriented.

**Pros:**
- Sleek, all-black colorway
- Comfortable for casual wear
- Unique and stylish design

**Cons:**
- Heavier than expected, not ideal for running
- Sizing may feel slightly off for those who prefer a snug fit

**Overall:** I would purchase these again, but not as my go-to running shoes. They're perfect for daily wear, but if you're a runner, you might want to look elsewhere.

For a legacy shoe, with a simple build, that's sold more units than I could count, it's surprising that their QC is so poor.

I purchased the Black/Black colorway and the effect is mostly complementary, more-so if you have a sportier style.

Good:

Tried a pair of Ava Rovers out, and I was surprised at how comfortable they are. The ReactX foam feels so soft, yet not too soft, and manages to cushion each step. Some of the other reviews mention ordering a size up, I fit in my normal size of 15 with no issues, although my feet are not of above average width. The fit is amazing, when you put them on it feels like sliding gloves on your feet. They offer great traction, on wet surfaces they got excellent grip and stability. Ava Rovers are lightweight as well, you almost forget you have shoes on while wearing them. 

The colorways are great too but the pictures on the website are a bit misleading. The Black/Muslin pair, the sole looks way more of an off-white color, while on the website it appears to be more of a light tan color. They ended up looking even better than on the website. I even picked up a pair in Phantom/Light Bone, and the website image was misleading again. They appeared to be a shrimp colored upper with a white sole. The shoe I received had a white upper and light gray sole, which was once again even better than expected. 

Concerns:

Tread on the sole looks a little thin compared to my DNs and other shoes. Hopefully future revisions have an option for thicker tread at the cost of a little more weight if durability turns out to be an issue. Also more reflective details would be nice, since they are only on the heel, wearing pants could cover them up. Finally I wish the laces were a bit thicker.

Great shoes, will be buying a third pair when additional colorways are released. Keep em coming lol.

raw_review_text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] [At a Glance]
   Right out of the box these new Ava Rover sneakers from Nike make a bold statement - bright, tri-tone colors blend smoothly together in five different types of material, with waves of texture that evoke a modern style. Swoosh is vibrantly colored and placed on the outer upper where it’s easy to see. Silhouette looks hefty, but speedy. 

   Definitely a unique design, but put together in a thoughtful way; not the kind of tasteless indulgence some other brands get caught up in.


[Fit & Feel]
   The Rovers fit true to size. Snug, but comfortable both walking and when seated.  Soles have plenty of support for hard surfaces. Sturdy structure yet (I was surprised to find) very lightweight overall. Nobbby outsole gives solid traction on smooth surfaces. Upper feltlike material feels very breathable. Laces are well-made and well-strung. 

   One clever design feature worth mentioning is that the heel tab is subtly textured for enhanced grip - plus it adds a splash of color matching the brand logo. Looks cool, works great! 

   The only element I didn’t like is the texture band between heel and collar; it’s left with an upward-facing flap that will undoubtedly catch debris over time and likely add an unnecessarily visible point of wear & tear as it rubs against the cuff of denim jeans or any other sturdy pants. I’d suggest stitching the top edge of this band in a future version.


[Verdict]
   High quality materials and good craftsmanship top-to-bottom — you can be sure you’re getting Nike’s best work when you snag a pair of Avas. Their bold, modern, comfortable design will have you sporting colors you never thought you’d see yourself in. Great look with with both jeans and khakis. Do yourself a favor and take these for a spin!

New Balance has built a lot of clout around being the last big sneaker company still making shoes in the United States. That reputation matters — people like me buy into the brand because we want to support American jobs, American factories, and American craftsmanship. But when I looked closer at the 990v6, I felt more let down than proud.

The shoe is advertised as “Made in USA,” but the fine print says it’s only about 70% domestic value. That means almost a third of the materials and components are imported — and customers aren’t even told which ones. That’s not the kind of transparency I expect from a company that has built its image on patriotism and heritage.

Instead, it feels like New Balance is leaning on the clout of the label without delivering the full promise. I didn’t want to settle for “mostly American made” — I wanted to buy something I could wear with pride, knowing it was built start to finish right here.

New Balance, if you’re going to wave the flag and sell the story of Made in USA, then back it up. Give us the breakdown of what’s really American made. raw_review_text:
Quality of the shoe is what you would expect from Nike/Jordan; Fairly well made, with slight oddities in design.

I had been looking at the 6 Rings online for awhile, when I had the chance to experience them in person ( Factory store Pigeon Forge) while on vacation.  As the store was very busy, and customers putting shoes just any where they could, I had to resort to getting a staff member to locate a couple sizes (Normally wear 8.5M) as my normal size seemed a bit snug; I settled into a size 9 as THE perfect fit. These shoes fit like a glove; very form fitting. Shoes have a heel liner (Or whatever they call it), that takes a time or two of putting them on to get the hang of it, but nothing that too difficult to master.

Straight out of the box, with no break-in, I walked for hours and hours through Gatlinburg, Clingmans Dome (Improved pathes), and several smaller journeys; I am very impressed, they are comfortable.

I would love to see these made with just tumbled leather, instead of patent leather lowers; patent leather is a bit too shiny for my style, but then I guess these are geared toward a younger demographic (I'm 57).

Anyone considering these need to try a half or full size larger than their usual size, as these are a bit form fitting and feel small; for me, a half size larger than my regular size took care of things. These do not fit (Or feel) like more classic Nike/Jordan models (Speaking of AJ1 & AF1). Soles feel more substantial than most other AJs (or Dunks) I own, and absorbed walking impact fairly well.

Overall, these are shaping up to be one of my all time favorites.

[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Nike Cortez shoes are a great everyday shoe that looks great and feels great. The shoes have a great retro look with the large Nike logos and great upper shoe style.  I normally wear shoes that don’t stand out, but these shoes with their bright white leather, shiny Nike logos, and blue trim along the bottom make me proud to wear a shoe that does stand out.  I feel instantly younger wearing these cool looking shoes.

The fit of the shoes is very comfortable.  They are surprisingly roomy in the toe box even though they look slender in this area.  I’ve worn them all day, but primarily on days where I’m not on my feet all day.  I suspect they wouldn’t be comfortable if I was on my feet all day such as at a theme park or a zoo.  I suspect this based on the arch support being slightly less than I would like, and the midsole cushion not being quite as cushiony as I would like for a day completely on my feet on pavement.  

With that said, these shoes are still very comfortable to wear for your typical day.  They are not too hot, which was a concern since they have completely leather uppers.  The shoe interior is well cushioned and didn’t create any rubs on my foot.  The heel feels slightly loose, but not to the point where it feels like your heel is sliding around or going to get a blister.  I felt well supported in these shoes, and the tread seems to have great grip.

I’m very pleased with these shoes and would recommend them to anyone looking for a hip new athletic casual shoe to wear.  They have great style and also great comfort.  The retro tread style reminds me of something my grandparents wore, but in a way that doesn’t make me feel old, but instead trendy.  The only thing I would maybe change is the tread pattern.  It provides fantastic grip, but it also appears to have great grip for keeping mud in the tread.  I will need to make sure I wear these on dry days or pavement to prevent mud for getting stuck in the tread grooves.  That is a minor annoyance, and all in all I think these are great shoes.  Well done Nike!

Width is good - but order a half to a whole size larger, depending upon how close your current size fits.

Cheers
